nodes.description: Pdzd8 mutant mice have reduced hippocampal long-term potentiation under maximal (3x theta burst) stimulation but not under submaximal protocols, together with impaired long-term spatial memory; fly knockdown impairs long-term courtship memory. Only the LTP reduction is bound as a process here; the memory deficits are organism-level behaviour and are carried by the intellectual disability phenotype. The authors read the cognitive impairment as a synaptopathy.

nodes.description: PDZD8 is needed for ER-mitochondria contacts. In cortical neurons its loss stops mitochondria taking up calcium released from the ER after synaptic stimulation, so cytosolic calcium rises higher in dendrites.

evidence.reference_title: ER-mitochondria tethering by PDZD8 regulates Ca(2+) dynamics in mammalian neurons.
evidence.snippet: In neurons, PDZD8 was required for calcium ion (Ca2+) uptake by mitochondria after synaptically induced Ca2+-release from ER and thereby regulated cytoplasmic Ca2+ dynamics.

nodes.description: Without PDZD8-mediated lipid supply at ER-late endosome/lysosome contacts, endosome maturation fails. PDZD8- or protrudin-depleted mouse neurons form abnormal large vacuoles, and in Drosophila PDZD8 is needed for lysosome maturation and autophagic flux at these contacts.

evidence.reference_title: Protrudin and PDZD8 contribute to neuronal integrity by promoting lipid extraction required for endosome maturation.
evidence.snippet: Our results suggest that protrudin and PDZD8 cooperatively promote endosome maturation by mediating ER-LyLE tethering and lipid extraction at MCSs, thereby maintaining neuronal polarity and integrity.

evidence.reference_title: PDZD8 promotes autophagy at ER-lysosome membrane contact sites to regulate activity-dependent synaptic growth.
evidence.snippet: PDZD8 accelerates autophagic flux by promoting lysosome maturation at ER-late endosome/lysosome MCSs.

nodes.description: PDZD8 depletion reduces neurite outgrowth in cultured cells, disrupts neuronal polarity, and in Drosophila blocks activity-dependent synaptic bouton formation. Pdzd8 mutant mice have increased dendritic spine density and reduced adult neurogenesis.

evidence.snippet: Intellectual developmental disorder with autism and dysmorphic facies (IDDADF) is a rare syndromic intellectual disability (ID) caused by homozygous disruption of PDZD8 (PDZ domain-containing protein 8), an integral endoplasmic reticulum (ER) protein.

nodes.description: Both PDZD8 alleles carry a premature termination codon (p.Q30* in exon 1, p.Y298* in exon 2, p.S733* in the last exon). Any protein escaping nonsense-mediated decay would keep the ER transmembrane anchor but lack the C-terminal regions that bind protrudin, late-endosome/lysosome phospholipids and Rab7, so no functional full-length protein is expected. PDZD8's SMP domain binds and transfers glycerophospholipids and ceramides between membranes, and the protein tethers the ER to late endosomes/lysosomes and to mitochondria. These activities are the gene's established functions; they were not measured on the patient alleles.

evidence.reference_title: PDZD8 Disruption Causes Cognitive Impairment in Humans, Mice, and Fruit Flies.

evidence.snippet: If a PTC-bearing allele does escape detection by NMD, protein translation would stop prematurely, and thus no functional full-length PDZD8 protein would be produced.

evidence.snippet: Furthermore, we discover that the SMP domain of PDZD8 binds glycerophospholipids and ceramides both in vivo and in vitro, and that the SMP domain can transport lipids between membranes in vitro.

evidence.snippet: Here we show that PDZD8, an intrinsic membrane protein of the ER with a lipid transport module of the SMP domain family, concentrates at contacts between the ER and late endosomes/lysosomes, where it interacts with GTP-Rab7.
